title: workload-shape-headroom-matrix-quicklook
body:
Purpose:
Quick, actionable capacity headroom matrix to feed Optimize cost models and inform a short A/B of autoscale thresholds. Working spreadsheet snapshot — rough numbers, want feedback from infra and SRE before we lock rates into the cost tool.

High level notes (to self / TL;DR):
- Focus: multi-region workload shapes (NA, EU, APAC) and burst vs baseline headroom.
- Deliverable: a compact matrix of % headroom by pool + marginal token cost at high-percentile concurrency to plug into the cost model.
- Status: draft assumptions included; run sensitivity on +/-20% demand and spot availability.

Assumptions (base case):
- Baseline Q4 app traffic projection: +38% tokens vs current month (source: GTM forecast dec 2025).
- Request mix: 62% short prompts (<=128 tokens), 28% medium (128-1024), 10% long (>1024).
- 95th percentile concurrency sampled from prod traces (Nov 2025): NA=420, EU=190, APAC=60.
- Serving pools: hosted-general (A100-40GB equiv), hosted-lowcost (A10x2 quantized operator), dedicated-shared (customer-dedicated RTX8000 equiv).
- Warmup for model variants: 0.8x KV cache hit expected for repeated sessions; prefix caching applied where applicable.

Matrix: (rows = region x pool; columns ~ baseline cap, 95p concurrency, estimated headroom %, marginal per-token cost)
CSV-like table (easy to paste into sheet):
region,pool,baseline_instances,95p_concurrency,baseline_capacity_tokens_per_min,estimated_headroom_pct,marginal_per_1k_tokens_usd
NA,hosted-general,24,420,1_800_000,12,0.0098
NA,hosted-lowcost,12,420,600_000,5,0.0061
EU,hosted-general,10,190,750_000,16,0.0112
EU,hosted-lowcost,6,190,300_000,7,0.0065
APAC,hosted-general,4,60,300_000,22,0.0105
APAC,hosted-lowcost,2,60,120_000,8,0.0068
NA,dedicated-shared,8,420,900_000,4,0.0135

Notes on numbers above:
- baseline_capacity_tokens_per_min estimated using average throughput per instance given current batching profiles (see infra/throughput-runbook).
- estimated_headroom_pct uses 95p concurrency relative to concurrent slots * avg tokens/sec per slot; conservative reductions for tail latency SLOs (reserve 10% for p99 fallbacks).
- marginal_per_1k_tokens_usd is blended from GPU amortized cost + network + orchestration + ephemeral storage. Lowcost pools assume more quantization (4-bit) and smaller kernel perf.

Scaling cost sensitivity (quick scenarios):
- Scenario A (demand +20%): NA hosted-general headroom drops from 12% -> 1.5% (forced to scale by 2 instances), marginal_per_1k_tokens_usd increases +8% due to lower packing efficiency.
- Scenario B (spot/lowcost partial outage 30% of capacity): reroute triggers to hosted-general and dedicated-shared; average marginal cost increases +26% regionally.
- Scenario C (quantize additional 2 bits on hosted-general for medium prompts): reduces marginal cost by ~14% but increases p99 latency for long prompts — risk flagged for product.

Break-even simple rule (for dedicated reservations):
- If projected stable monthly token volume for a customer pool > 1.2B tokens/month AND 95p concurrency requires > 6 dedicated instances steady-state, recommend reserved capacity commit.
- Simple calc: reserved_monthly_cost / (on-demand_marginal_savings_per_token * projected_tokens) < 12 months -> commit.

Quick ops playbook (operationalizing into Optimize):
- Input matrix to Optimize: region/pool/headroom/marginal costs as parameters; run existing cost-sim with +/−20% demand bands. Note: file id for cost-sim config: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/configs/headroom-v3 (PR pending).
- Autoscale rule suggestions (draft):
  * Expand when 95p concurrency > 85% of pool capacity for > 5 consecutive minutes.
  * Shrink when 50p concurrency < 60% for > 10 minutes and p99 latency within SLO.
  * Prefer vertical scale (increase instances of same pool) before fallback to higher-cost pool unless headroom < 3%.
- Canary rollout: enable new autoscale thresholds in NA hosted-lowcost week 1 for 48h, track p99, cost delta, cache hit rate.

Open questions / risks (talking points for infra sync):
- How many tokens per second can we realistically squeeze from an A100 equiv with the new attention-kernel? Our perf bench conjures different numbers for short vs long (See INF-4237).
- Impact of aggressive quantization on hallucination rates (needs product evaluation).
- Cross-region burst routing latency — can cause dropped sessions if fallback route > 200ms RTT.
- Accounting edge-case: when mixing reserved and spot, true marginal cost per token becomes non-linear; Optimize needs stepwise pricing curves.

References / links (copy into Confluence after review):
- Raw trace slice (Nov 2025) -> jira JIRA-INF-4512.
- Autoscale rule draft -> github.com/redwood-inference/infra/ops/autoscale-rules.md (PR #1299).
- Prior headroom workbook (do not overwrite): shared_drives/product/optimize/capacity-runway-scenarios-cumulative-costs.json

Immediate next steps (owner assignments):
- Priya: finalize marginal cost calc by Feb 5 2026 (pending infra perf numbers).
- Mateo: run +20% and spot-outage sensitivity sims in local Optimize fork (JIRA-INF-4321).
- Jia: prepare short UX brief for product on risk tradeoffs for quantization by Feb 12.
- Riley: schedule infra sync, include SRE to vet autoscale thresholds.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc narrow — this is an input to the cost model, not the final recommendation. When numbers converge, produce a one-pager with clear commit recommendation for Dedicated reservations and recommended autoscale policy changes.

Changelog (quick):
- 2025-11-20: created initial matrix and assumptions (Priya).
- 2025-12-10: updated marginal costs after initial infra run (Mateo).
- 2026-02-28: revised headroom numbers after November->Jan traffic rebaseline and added sensitivity scenarios (this file).

Unstructured scratch (important snippets):
- formula for headroom pct: headroom_pct = max( (baseline_capacity_tokens_per_min - tokens_needed_for_95p) / baseline_capacity_tokens_per_min * 100, 0 ).
- tokens_needed_for_95p = 95p_concurrency * avg_tokens_per_request * avg_req_per_min_per_slot_estimate
- rough avg_tokens_per_request per bucket: short=64, medium=420, long=1800 (weighted above).

End of snapshot.

ACTION: If you copy this into a Google Sheet, keep the CSV block in a separate tab named 'matrix-quicklook' and label the sheet with date (2026-02-28) and owner initials (PN).
